learning_outcomes.text: When this course will finish, student will learn basic properties, related terms and principles of compressible flows, and can analysis these flows.
Can apply first and second laws of thermodynamics.
Can solve supersonic flows problems in converging nozzles.
Can solve flows problems in converging diverging channels.
Can analysis the creation case of shock waves.

syllabus_topics: BASIC CONCEPTS AND LAWS: Definitions, Classification of flows, Mass balance, First and second laws of Newton.
BASIC CONCEPTS AND LAWS: First and second laws of Thermodynamics, stagnation, sonic velocity, Mach number.
BASIC PROPERTIES OF STEADY AND ONE DIMENSIONAL COMPRESSIBLE FLOWS: Derivative of basic balances for ideal gases as Mach Number function. Total balances as a Mach Number function.
ADIABATIC FLOWS IN VARIABLE CROSS-SECTION: Frictionless flows. Flows of ideal fluids, Term of referance and usage of isentropic tables.
ADIABATIC FLOWS IN VARIABLE CROSS-SECTION: Flows in difusers and nozzles.
STAGNANT NORMAL SHOCK WAVES: Analysis of stagnanat normal shock waves for fluids and ideal gases. Usage of normal shock waves table.
STAGNANT NORMAL SHOCK WAVES: Stagnant shock waves in nozzles. Wind tunnels.
DYNAMIC NORMAL SHOCK WAVES: Analysis of dynamic normal shock waves.
OBLIQUE SHOCK WAVES: Analysis of oblique shock waves, ideal gases tables and reading of graphics for oblique shock waves.
STEADY ONE DIMENSIONAL FRICTIONAL FLOWS (FANNO FLOWS) : Derivative of thermodynamics formulas, Usage of fanno curves and tables for ideal gases.
NON-ADIABATIC FLOWS (RAYLEIGH FLOWS): Derivative of thermodynamics formulas, Usage of Rayleigh curves and tables for ideal gases.
NON-ADIABATIC FLOWS (RAYLEIGH FLOWS): Derivative of thermodynamics formulas, Usage of Rayleigh curves and tables for ideal gases.
JET SYSTEMS: Rockets and jet motors.
bibliography: Compressible Fluid Dynamics with PC Applications, B. K. Hodge and K. Koenig, Prentice Hall, 1995.
